chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about an animal that was slaughtered facing other than the qiblah, and he said:
"Eat; there is no harm in that so long as it was not done intentionally."

He said: And I asked him about a man who slaughtered and did not mention the name of Allah. He said: "If he had forgotten, then let him mention it when he remembers, saying: In the name of Allah, at its beginning and at its end."

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the qiblah, the prescribed direction relevant to ritual practice
key_terms.يُتَعَمَّدْ: to be done deliberately or intentionally
key_terms.يُسَمِّ: to mention the name of Allah at slaughter

ai.seo_question: Is slaughter valid if the animal was not faced toward the qiblah or if Allah's name was forgotten?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning slaughter. If an animal is slaughtered facing other than the qiblah unintentionally, there is no harm in eating it; likewise, if the slaughterer forgot the tasmiyah, he should mention the name of Allah when he remembers.
